summary: Bounded NUL-terminated string copy with destination padding. Copies at most a3 bytes from source a2 to destination a1; stops at the terminating zero byte and, when room remains within the count, fills the rest of the destination with zero bytes. Returns a1. Fast path copies whole dwords using an embedded-zero detection mask (0x81010100 test on (word + 2130640639) ^ word ^ 0xFFFFFFDE) and a byte-at-a-time fallback for unaligned sources. Callers are string/file-path and name-copy routines.

local_names.v5: source pointer (a2) advanced as bytes are consumed
local_names.v6: destination pointer (a1) advanced as bytes are written
local_names.v11: dword zero-detection mask result for the word-at-a-time fast path
local_names.v12: dword loaded from source in the fast path

operations.description: Guard on copy count: when a3 is zero, return a1 immediately without touching the destination.
Guard on source alignment: when a2 is 4-byte aligned the word-at-a-time fast path is used; otherwise a byte-by-byte loop copies until the source becomes aligned.
Byte copy loop: read *v5++, write *v6++, stop on a zero terminator byte or when the remaining count (v4/v3) is exhausted; on early terminator the remaining slots of the destination are zero-padded.
Fast-path zero detection: v11 = (word + 2130640639) ^ word ^ 0xFFFFFFDE; a non-zero (v11 & 0x81010100) indicates an embedded zero byte within the loaded 4-byte word.
Fast-path terminator position: inspect the loaded word for zero in byte 0, byte 1 ((v12 & 0xFF0000) == 0), or byte 2 ((v12 & 0xFF000000) == 0) and keep only the bytes before the terminator.
Fast path writes the truncated word (1, 2 or 3 bytes, or a full dword when no terminator is present) into the destination and advances v6 by 4.
After a terminator, pad the destination with zero bytes for the remainder of the count: dword stores of 0 while count permits, then the leftover 0 to 3 bytes.
Return a1, the destination buffer, on every exit path.
